review: The hymn is a litany of 'none but You': 1:1–3 is Ps 73:25–26 with Isa 26:3, 2:1–3 is Ps 34:9 with Ps 119:105, 3:1–3 is Ps 16:11 with Ps 94:19, 4:1–3 is Song 2:2 with Ps 147:3, and 5:1–3 is Ps 91:1 with Ps 18:2.

The vocative אֲדֹנִי ends the first two lines of every stanza, exactly as the print ends them with يَا سَيِّدِي; the payload repeats it in all ten places rather than letting it fall away, because the address is the form of the hymn.

2:2 מַחְשַׁבְתִּי לֹא שְׁכָחַתְךָ — the Arabic فِكْرِي مَا سَلَاك is 'my thought never forgot You'; the Hebrew uses שָׁכַח with the object suffix, since the Arabic's verb is the forgetting one and a smoother 'I never ceased to think of You' would lose the negated memory.
